flags.title: California residents only
flags.body: COSMOS accepts students completing grades 8–12 who are enrolled in a California high school. Out-of-state students are not eligible.
flags.sourceCitation: COSMOS statewide eligibility requirements (UC COSMOS)

flags.title: $200 deposit non-refundable
flags.body: A $200 deposit is required to hold a spot and is non-refundable — including for students who receive full financial aid.
flags.sourceCitation: COSMOS program fee and deposit policy

flags.title: ~4% acceptance rate
flags.body: MIT RSI accepts approximately 4% of applicants globally. Admission is among the most competitive of any U.S. pre-college program.
flags.sourceCitation: Center for Excellence in Education / RSI program materials

flags.title: PSAT Math 740+ practical floor
flags.body: While not a published cutoff, successful applicants typically score PSAT Math 740 or higher. Strong math and science preparation is effectively required.
flags.sourceCitation: RSI applicant guidance and alumni admissions patterns

flags.title: Fully funded for accepted students
flags.body: All accepted RSI students attend tuition-free. Room, board, and program costs are covered for admitted participants.
flags.sourceCitation: RSI program fee policy (CEE)

flags.title: SEVP certification terminated
flags.body: Harvard SSP's SEVP certification was terminated in May 2025. International students must verify current visa and enrollment eligibility directly with Harvard before applying.
flags.sourceCitation: U.S. Department of Homeland Security SEVP announcement, May 2025

flags.title: 55% campus crime rate increase (2022–2023)
flags.body: Harvard reported a 55% increase in campus crime between 2022 and 2023. Review the university's Annual Security Report when evaluating a residential summer enrollment.
flags.sourceCitation: Harvard University Annual Security Report (Clery Act)

flags.title: Historical abuse allegations and donor history
flags.body: Interlochen has faced historical abuse allegations, underwent an external investigation, and received donations from Jeffrey Epstein from 1990 to 2003. Review recent safety reporting and institutional responses before enrolling.
flags.sourceCitation: Public reporting, external investigation findings, and institutional disclosures

flags.title: Mandatory solo wilderness camping
flags.body: Outward Bound courses require a solo wilderness camping period, typically 24–72 hours, as a core part of the curriculum.
flags.sourceCitation: Outward Bound USA course structure and participant requirements

flags.title: Middle School commuters cannot attend evening or off-campus activities
flags.body: Unlike the High School commuter track, Middle School commuter students at UCLA are explicitly excluded from evening programming and off-campus excursions.
flags.sourceCitation: summerapply.com Middle School Enrichment Programs at UCLA listing (secondary source, not the primary Summer Discovery site directly)

flags.title: $550 non-refundable deposit
flags.body: Wake Forest requires a $550 non-refundable deposit in addition to tuition.
flags.sourceCitation: Wake Forest Summer Immersion fee schedule

flags.title: No parent contact during the trip
flags.body: Guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to families. Parents should expect zero direct communication with their child for the length of the trip barring an actual emergency.
flags.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Olympic National Park summer camp FAQ

flags.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures 10-Day Mammoth to Yosemite Teen Adventure program page

flags.title: Trip may be restructured if enrollment is low
flags.body: Terms & Conditions require a minimum of 6 participants for the 20-day leadership expedition. If enrollment falls short, Lasting Adventures may restructure the session into consecutive 13-day and 6-day trips instead.
flags.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Terms & Conditions

flags.title: Trip may be restructured if enrollment is low
flags.body: Terms & Conditions require a minimum of 6 participants for the 20-day leadership expedition. If enrollment falls short, Lasting Adventures may restructure the session into consecutive 13-day and 6-day trips instead.
flags.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Terms & Conditions

flags.title: One-week Intensives are not eligible for financial aid
flags.body: Interlochen's one-week High School Intensive programs are excluded from the camp's financial aid program, even though longer sessions may qualify.
flags.sourceCitation: Interlochen High School theatre intake and org-wide Intensive policy

flags.title: Focus Programs (Veterinary Science, Medical Rotations) exclude rising 7th graders
flags.body: Unlike EXPLO 360, which is open to the full rising 7-9 grade band, both Focus Programs are restricted to rising 8th and 9th graders only. A rising 7th grader can only enroll in EXPLO 360.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO 2027 registration form

flags.title: "4 weeks" is not a distinct product - it's enrolling in both sessions
flags.body: The registration form only lists 2-week Session 1 and Session 2 options; a family wanting the full 4 weeks selects Session 1, completes payment, then is prompted to separately select Session 2. A Double Session Discount applies ($500 overnight/$300 day per the 2026 schedule) but there is no single bundled '4-week' product.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO 2027 registration form instructions

flags.title: Extra fee for unaccompanied-minor airport service, and a caution against flying that way
flags.body: EXPLO explicitly recommends students NOT fly as unaccompanied minors unless required by the airline, and charges an extra $150 each way if a family does use EXPLO's transportation for an unaccompanied minor.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO Tuition + Financial Aid page

flags.title: Pre-med / health careers focus track
flags.body: Medical Rotations is EXPLO Middle School's pre-med oriented Focus Program: a fixed curriculum shadowing medical fields rather than the custom EXPLO 360 workshop menu. Rising 8th and 9th graders only.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO 2027 registration form (explo.org)

flags.title: Local Chapter vs National Chapter pricing - a real structural choice, not a discount code
flags.body: Prices vary by several hundred to over $1,000 depending on whether a family joins through a Local Chapter (community group fundraising) or applies individually as a National Chapter member. Montanas y Mar has no Local Chapter option at all.
flags.sourceCitation: AMIGOS Costs & Access page

flags.title: No Immerse (longest/deepest) tier offered in Panama
flags.body: Unlike Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, and Paraguay, Panama does not offer an Immerse-tier program - its longest option (El Valle) is 3 weeks, not 4-6.
flags.sourceCitation: AMIGOS Programs page

flags.title: No routine parent contact during the trip
flags.body: Consistent with the 'unplugged' program philosophy, families should not expect regular calls, texts, or updates from their student during the trip itself.
flags.sourceCitation: Moondance Adventures general FAQ pages

flags.title: Price has an unresolved footnote
flags.body: The $10,995 price on the source page carries a double-asterisk linking to explanatory text that wasn't captured in this research pass - worth confirming directly before treating the figure as final.
flags.sourceCitation: Moondance Adventures Mystery Trip page

flags.title: Prices reflect a limited-time early enrollment discount
flags.body: The org's site banner advertises a $300 early bird discount through 9/20 (2026) for 2027 enrollment - the prices captured may not reflect the later standard rate.
flags.sourceCitation: Apogee Adventures site banner

flags.title: Requires an existing PADI certification to enroll
flags.body: This program requires students to already hold a specific PADI certification level (Open Water, Rescue Diver, etc.) before enrolling - it is not a beginner-friendly option despite being open enrollment otherwise.
flags.sourceCitation: Broadreach program pages

flags.title: Restricted to returning Broadreach students only
flags.body: This program is not open to first-time Broadreach applicants regardless of grade, age, or certification level - it exclusively serves alumni of prior Broadreach programs.
flags.sourceCitation: Broadreach Belize Alumni-Only Advanced Scuba program page

flags.title: Liveaboard vs. land-based format not explicitly confirmed
flags.body: Unlike every other Broadreach program, this one's source page didn't explicitly state 'liveaboard' or 'land-based' in the captured content. Placed in the land-based day-to-day group based on its rainforest/reef description, but worth confirming directly.
flags.sourceCitation: Broadreach Belize Alumni-Only Advanced Scuba program page

flags.title: Minimum age 15 required, independent of grade
flags.body: This program requires students to be at least 15 years old at the time of the program, which could exclude a young student in an otherwise-eligible grade.
flags.sourceCitation: Broadreach Fiji Shark Studies program page

flags.title: Requires an existing PADI Open Water certification to enroll
flags.body: This program requires students to already hold PADI Open Water certification (or equivalent) before enrolling - not a beginner-friendly option despite the middle-school framing.
flags.sourceCitation: Broadreach middle school program pages

flags.title: Must be 12 years old by program start
flags.body: In addition to the completing-grades band, students must be at least 12 years old by the program start date — a student in an eligible grade who has not yet turned 12 would not qualify.
flags.sourceCitation: Broadreach middle school program pages

flags.title: No on-campus housing, even for the in-person option
flags.body: Unlike WPI's Frontiers program, this program does not provide on-campus housing under any format - a family choosing the in-person option needs to arrange their own housing or have the student commute from home.
flags.sourceCitation: WPI High-Achieving High School Students program page

flags.title: Eligibility depends on family home address, not school location
flags.body: A student's eligibility is based on where their family's permanent home address is (must be in the US year-round), not where they attend school. This means a student at a US boarding school with a family home abroad is ineligible, while a student at a boarding school abroad with a US family home is eligible.
flags.sourceCitation: MIT WTP FAQ page

flags.title: Enrolled students must complete online prerequisite coursework before the in-person/virtual session starts
flags.body: Being accepted isn't the end of the work: enrolled students must finish the graded online prerequisite course by a deadline in mid-to-late June (shown as June 18 on the 2027 program timeline) - missing this puts a student's summer spot at risk, per BWSI's own admissions messaging.
flags.sourceCitation: User-provided 2027 program timeline graphic

flags.title: No online courses or other programs allowed during camp
flags.body: HSMC explicitly prohibits campers from taking any online courses or participating in any other program - in person or virtual - for the full six weeks. Families should not plan for a student to double up on summer commitments.
flags.sourceCitation: Mathworks HSMC program page

flags.title: No online courses or other programs allowed during camp
flags.body: Unlike most residential summer programs, JSMCR explicitly prohibits campers from taking any online courses or participating in any other program - in person or virtual - for the full two weeks. Families should not plan for a student to double up on summer commitments.
flags.sourceCitation: Mathworks JSMCR program page

flags.title: No partial attendance or early departure permitted
flags.body: Students must attend from the first day to the last day of the three-week program with no exceptions - the program explicitly states this is required because college credit is awarded for the full session. Families with a conflicting commitment (e.g., another camp, a family trip) cannot plan around a partial stay.
flags.sourceCitation: M&TSI FAQs page

flags.title: The $12,000 fee doesn't cover the following:
flags.body: Not included in the program fee: the $100 non-refundable application fee, travel to/from Philadelphia, Pottruck Gym access, off-campus meals (including all Saturdays, when no meals are provided at all), medical expenses, laundry, and personal spending money.
flags.sourceCitation: M&TSI program page, fee breakdown

flags.title: Org's own pages disagree on whether tuition covers 3 meals a day
flags.body: The general Oxford Academia FAQ page states Yale tuition 'includes all accommodations and three meals each day,' but the Yale-specific program page states lunches are not included in tuition and are handled independently by students. Families should confirm directly which is accurate before budgeting.
flags.sourceCitation: Oxford Academia FAQ page vs. Yale program page (both oxfordacademia.com)

flags.title: Tuition (once published) will exclude several real costs
flags.body: Per the general FAQ: the $200 non-refundable application fee, airfare/travel to the program, lunches, classroom/art supplies, laundry, communication home, health care, and personal expenses are all separate from tuition. Airport group transportation to campus (JFK or Bradley) costs $65 each way if used.
flags.sourceCitation: Oxford Academia FAQ page

flags.title: Meals are not included in the Manhattan residential fee
flags.body: Unlike SOCAPA's Los Angeles and Vermont campuses, where room & board includes three daily meals Mon-Fri, Manhattan residential students must purchase their own meals for the entire session (with brief counselor guidance the first three days only). Families should budget separately for food.
flags.sourceCitation: SOCAPA Tuition & Costs page

flags.title: Lunch is not included in tuition, despite meals being advertised as covered
flags.body: Program pages list breakfast and dinner as included, but lunch is explicitly excluded and paid for independently by students each day - worth budgeting for separately.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA program pages, 'What's Included' section

flags.title: Advertised price includes a limited-time discount
flags.body: The prices shown ($6,399 for 14 days, $8,599 for 21 days, $11,499 for 27 days with Hawaii) reflect active 'enroll early and save' promotions off list prices of $6,699, $8,999, and $11,999 respectively. The discount is time-limited and not guaranteed to still apply later in the enrollment cycle.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA program pages (14-, 21-, and 27-day)

flags.title: Not a UCLA-run program despite the branding
flags.body: The program page includes an explicit disclaimer: this is operated by Westcoast Connection, not UCLA. Students stay in UCLA housing and use UCLA facilities, and some instructors are UCLA Extension faculty, but 'responsibility for the program resides solely with Westcoast Connection.'
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA 14-day, 21-day, and 27-day program pages

flags.title: $850 internal Hawaii flights not included in tuition
flags.body: Beyond airfare to Los Angeles and home from Oahu, the program charges an additional $850 for internal flights from Los Angeles to Hawaii and between the Hawaiian islands.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA plus Hawaii Extension program page

flags.title: Round-trip airfare to/from the program not included
flags.body: Tuition does not include flights to Los Angeles at the start or your return flight home from Oahu. Optional chaperoned group flights may be available from the New York area.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA plus Hawaii Extension program page

flags.title: No commuter option for the Hawaii extension
flags.body: This 27-day itinerary is residential only — there is no day-student or commuter enrollment for the combined UCLA and Hawaii program.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA plus Hawaii Extension program page

flags.title: Commuter is a distinct schedule, not residential in day format
flags.body: The commuter option covers class days only across three non-consecutive weeks — not the full 21-day residential session with overnight and weekend programming.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA Pre-College Commuter Option section

flags.title: No meals included for commuter students
flags.body: Commuter tuition does not include any meals. Students should plan for breakfast, lunch, and dinner on class days.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA Pre-College Commuter Option section

flags.title: Limited recreational facility access
flags.body: Commuter students have limited access to UCLA's recreational facilities compared to residential participants.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA Pre-College Commuter Option section

flags.title: Grade band shown as two ranges - cohort assignment not confirmed
flags.body: This program lists grades as '6th-8th | 9th-12th' rather than a single range, suggesting parallel middle-school and high-school groups run on the same dates. It's not confirmed from the source whether these are truly separate cohorts or one combined group spanning the full range - worth confirming directly.
flags.sourceCitation: ARCC program pages

flags.title: Age range sourced from third party, not directly confirmed
flags.body: A recent comparison source states this program is open to ages 13-18, a notably wider range than ARCC's typical '9th-12th current grade' pattern. This wasn't independently confirmed via a direct ARCC page fetch and is worth verifying before treating as final.
flags.sourceCitation: Third-party comparison site (rusticpathways.com)

flags.title: Need-based Global Navigator scholarship not available
flags.body: Only the CIEE Academic Merit Award applies to this program. The standard CIEE Global Navigator Scholarship (need-based) is explicitly not available here — important for families relying on need-based aid.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Fashion Marketing in Europe program page

flags.title: Program moves through three cities in three countries
flags.body: This is a traveling program: students spend time in Paris, Milan, and Madrid within a single three-week session, with travel and border crossings built into the itinerary. Families should confirm passport/visa requirements cover all three countries.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Fashion Marketing in Europe (Paris/Milan/Madrid) program page, Overview and Destination sections

flags.title: Correction: Belgium does have a CIEE High School Summer Abroad program
flags.body: An earlier pass concluded Belgium had no standalone summer program, based on blog posts describing Brussels only as an excursion destination. That was incorrect - Diplomacy & Government (Brussels) is a genuine, newly-launched 2027 program. The excursion-themed blog posts were describing trips FROM the related Amsterdam/Tallinn programs, which coincidentally visit Brussels as part of their own itineraries.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Diplomacy & Government (Brussels) program page

flags.title: Must have completed Freshman year before travel
flags.body: CIEE requires students to have completed Freshman year of high school before traveling on this program — a rising freshman would not yet qualify.

flags.title: Cannot accommodate fully Kosher or Halal diets

flags.body: CIEE's term selector marks Session II as 'TBD,' but the Dates & Fees table on the same page lists specific dates with an apparent typo (end date shown as 'July 31, 3027'). Families should confirm exact Session II dates directly with CIEE before booking flights.

flags.title: Moderate- to high-intensity physical activity expected
flags.body: CIEE's own eligibility notes describe this program as involving moderate- to high-intensity physical activities such as hiking, boating, and snorkeling. Swimming ability is not required but is strongly encouraged to fully participate in the program's water-based fieldwork.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Marine Ecology & Sustainability (Lisbon) program page, Eligibility section

flags.title: Significant daily athletic commitment expected
flags.body: CIEE's own eligibility notes say prior soccer experience (school, club, or rec) is preferred, and students should be prepared for daily practice/training sessions of up to 3 hours, five days a week — a heavier physical commitment than CIEE's academic or creative-arts programs.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Soccer & Mental Performance (Lisbon) program page, Eligibility section

flags.title: Cannot accommodate fully Vegetarian, Kosher, or Vegan diets
flags.body: CIEE states this program cannot accommodate a fully Vegetarian, Kosher, or Vegan diet, due to the local cuisine and available food options — a broader dietary exclusion list than CIEE's other Marine Ecology & Sustainability offerings (e.g., Lisbon, Mérida), which only exclude Kosher/Halal.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Marine Ecology & Sustainability (San Juan) program page, Eligibility section

flags.title: Moderate- to high-intensity physical activity expected

flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Marine Ecology & Sustainability (San Juan) program page, Eligibility section

flags.title: No price published yet for 2027
flags.body: Unlike CIEE's other Edinburgh programs, this page does not display a cost for either Summer Session I or II as of this research pass — only dates and the $25 application fee are shown. Families should contact CIEE directly for current pricing before applying.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Golf & Mental Performance (Edinburgh) program page, Dates & Fees section

flags.title: Moderate-intensity physical activity expected

flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Korean Language & Culture (Seoul) program page, Dates & Fees section

flags.title: South Korea has strict medication import regulations
flags.body: CIEE notes that South Korea maintains strict regulations on medications brought into the country and encourages families to consult their doctor and confirm the student's medications are legal and available there before traveling.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Diplomacy & Government in East Asia (Seoul/Taipei) program page, Eligibility section

flags.title: Need-based scholarship is not available for this program
flags.body: CIEE states that only the Academic Merit Award applies to this program; the need-based Global Navigator Scholarship (GNS) is not available here. Families seeking need-based aid for a similar diplomacy program are pointed to CIEE's Tallinn, Estonia offering instead.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Diplomacy & Government in East Asia (Seoul/Taipei) program page, Overview section

flags.title: Dietary restrictions likely to reduce program engagement
flags.body: CIEE's own page includes an explicit warning that dietary restrictions will likely reduce a student's ability to engage in the full content of the program courses, since the program's content is built around cooking and eating.

flags.title: Requires a pre-program Spanish proficiency test
flags.body: This Honors program is gated by a pre-program STAMP language proficiency test. Students must have completed high school Spanish Level 2 or higher and score at least Intermediate-Low on the ACTFL scale; those who do not meet the bar may be moved to a standard (non-Honors) Language & Culture program instead. Students who don't yet meet the criteria are directed to apply to the standard programs in Barcelona, Madrid, Palma, Seville, Buenos Aires, or Merida as a second choice.
flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Honors Spanish Language & Culture (Madrid) program page, Eligibility section

flags.title: Session I dates are not yet published for 2027

flags.sourceCitation: CIEE Honors Spanish Language & Culture (Madrid) program page, Dates & Fees section

flags.title: Requires a pre-program Spanish proficiency test
flags.body: Since this program is taught entirely in Spanish, participants must place at the Intermediate-Mid level or higher on the STAMP 4S proficiency test (taken in spring before departure) and have completed high school Spanish Level 3 or higher, or be able to fully participate in an oral interview in Spanish at that level. Students who do not place high enough may be moved to the English-taught version of the program instead.
